Draw samples from the posterior distribution of an estimated model

Source: R/diagnostic-posterior.R, R/gamm4-methods.R, R/posterior-samples.R
posterior_samples.Rd

Draw samples from the posterior distribution of an estimated model

Usage

# S3 method for class 'lm'
posterior_samples(model, ..., n_draws = NULL, seed = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'glm'
posterior_samples(model, ..., n_draws = NULL, seed = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'glmmTMB'
posterior_samples(model, ..., n_draws = NULL, seed = NULL, conditioning = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'sdmTMB'
posterior_samples(model, ..., n_draws = NULL, seed = NULL, conditioning = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'gamlss'
posterior_samples(model, ..., n_draws = NULL, seed = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'gamm'
posterior_samples(model, ..., n_draws = NULL, seed = NULL, conditioning = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'lme'
posterior_samples(model, ..., n_draws = NULL, seed = NULL, conditioning = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'merMod'
posterior_samples(model, ..., n_draws = NULL, seed = NULL, conditioning = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'gamm4'
posterior_samples(model, ..., n_draws = NULL, seed = NULL, conditioning = NULL)

posterior_samples(model, ...)

# S3 method for class 'gam'
posterior_samples(
  model,
  ...,
  data = NULL,
  n_draws = NULL,
  chains = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  method = c("gaussian", "mh", "inla", "user"),
  n_cores = 1L,
  n_threads = 1L,
  burnin = 1000,
  thin = 1L,
  t_df = 40,
  rw_scale = 0.25,
  frequentist = FALSE,
  unconditional = FALSE,
  draws = NULL,
  diagnostics = FALSE,
  mh_backend = c("mgcv", "gratia", "family"),
  mvn_method = c("mvnfast", "mgcv"),
  block_size = 10000L,
  dense_limit = 5e+06,
  weights = NULL,
  family_index = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'scam'
posterior_samples(
  model,
  ...,
  data = NULL,
  n_draws = NULL,
  chains = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  method = c("gaussian", "mh", "inla", "user"),
  n_cores = 1L,
  n_threads = 1L,
  burnin = 1000,
  thin = 1L,
  t_df = 40,
  rw_scale = 0.25,
  frequentist = FALSE,
  unconditional = FALSE,
  draws = NULL,
  diagnostics = FALSE,
  mh_backend = c("mgcv", "gratia", "family"),
  mvn_method = c("mvnfast", "mgcv"),
  block_size = 10000L,
  dense_limit = 5e+06,
  weights = NULL,
  family_index = NULL
)

Arguments

model

a fitted model of the supported types; see diagnostic_support.

...

arguments passed to other methods. For fitted_samples(), these are passed on to mgcv::predict.gam(). For posterior_samples() these are passed on to fitted_samples(). For predicted_samples() these are passed on to the relevant simulate() method.

n_draws

positive integer; total retained draws across all chains. Required when generating draws. With method = "user", the supplied matrix determines the count; an explicit count must agree with its rows.

seed

numeric; a random seed for the simulations.

conditioning

character or NULL; mixed-model conditioning mode; see diagnostic_support.

data

data frame; new observations at which the posterior draws from the model should be evaluated. If not supplied, the data used to fit the model will be used for data, if available in model.

chains

positive integer or NULL; number of chains. NULL uses one chain, or the chain mapping in supplied draws. n_draws must be divisible by chains. Burn-in is applied separately to each MH chain.

method

character; which method should be used to draw samples from the posterior distribution. "gaussian" uses a Gaussian (Laplace) approximation to the posterior. "mh" uses a Metropolis Hastings sampler that alternates t proposals with proposals based on a shrunken version of the posterior covariance matrix. "inla" uses a variant of Integrated Nested Laplace Approximation due to Wood (2019), (currently not implemented). "user" allows for user-supplied posterior draws as a coefficient matrix.

n_cores

positive integer; maximum concurrent MH chains using mirai, capped at chains. Existing workers are reused; otherwise temporary workers are created and cleaned up. Only used by method = "mh".

n_threads

positive integer; threads within Gaussian sampling using mvnfast. Defaults to one. This is separate from concurrent MH chains.

burnin

numeric; number of samples to discard as the burnin draws. Only used with method = "mh".

thin

positive integer; retain every thin iterations after burn-in.

t_df

numeric; degrees of freedom for t distribution proposals. Only used with method = "mh".

rw_scale

numeric; Factor by which to scale posterior covariance matrix when generating random walk proposals. Negative or non finite to skip the random walk step. Only used with method = "mh".

frequentist

logical; TRUE to use the frequentist covariance matrix of the parameter estimators, FALSE to use the Bayesian posterior covariance matrix of the parameters.

unconditional

logical; if TRUE (and frequentist == FALSE) then the Bayesian smoothing parameter uncertainty corrected covariance matrix is used, if available.

draws

matrix; user supplied posterior draws to be used when method = "user".

diagnostics

logical; calculate coefficient R-hat, effective sample sizes, and Monte Carlo standard errors using the optional posterior package.

mh_backend

character; "mgcv" preserves mgcv::gam.mh(). "gratia" uses compiled common-family likelihoods. "family" uses a compiled MH loop with callbacks to the fitted family object. Both support independent-observation bam fits. Smoothing parameters and parameters outside the fitted coefficient vector remain fixed. LSS scale and shape coefficients are sampled jointly with location. The family backend caches a full design matrix, smoothing penalty, and proposal factorisation once for all chains.

mvn_method

character; one of "mvnfast" or "mgcv". The default is uses mvnfast::rmvn(), which can be considerably faster at generate large numbers of MVN random values than mgcv::rmvn(), but which might not work for some marginal fits, such as those where the covariance matrix is close to singular.

block_size

positive integer; maximum observation rows per block in the gratia MH evaluator. Large designs are evaluated without storing a full matrix.

dense_limit

numeric; maximum number of design-matrix elements to cache for the gratia MH backend. Use zero to force blockwise evaluation.

weights

numeric; response sampling weights for GAM methods. An explicit vector overrides the fitting weights; a single value applies to every observation. With data = NULL, the default is the fitted prior weights, except factor-valued binomial responses retain one Bernoulli trial per observation. Native gaulss() ignores fitting weights in its likelihood, so its default response weights are also ones; explicitly supplied sampling weights still override this default. With prediction data, weights default to a vector of ones. For ordinary Gaussian and Gamma responses, larger weights reduce response variance (precision weights). For binomial responses, weights give integer trial counts. They do not alter the fitted coefficient covariance. Include positions restored by na.exclude when supplying weights for fitting rows.

family_index

numeric; optional family-list positions for grouped family (mgcv::gfam()) response draws, one integer per evaluation row. Membership can instead be recovered from the response-index expression in data; observed response values are not required.

Value

A tibble (data frame) in long format, with columns:

  • .row: row of the evaluation data;

  • .draw: globally unique draw identifier;

  • .response: simulated response. Where needed, .parameter identifies the response or grouped component. Multiple-chain output also includes .chain and .iteration. Attached coefficient diagnostics are available through sampling_diagnostics().

Details

The lm, glm, glmmTMB, GJRM::gamlss, sdmTMB, and full mixed-model diagnostic samplers currently use the fitting observations only. They draw coefficients together using Gaussian approximations. See posterior_predictive_plot() for which additional distribution parameters remain fixed and how random effects are treated for each fitter.

With no explicit data, observation rows follow the fitted model's na.action. na.exclude restores excluded rows as NA in every draw; na.omit returns retained rows only. .row indexes the fitting data after any subset. With explicit data, .row indexes that data, missing responses do not prevent prediction, and missing required predictors give NA draws. An explicit prediction na.action in ... is honoured without renumbering retained rows. Restoration does not consume random numbers.

For Gaussian identity-link bam and scam fits, first-order autoregressive (AR1) errors make consecutive responses correlated. Responses are drawn together to retain this fitted correlation, restarting at each AR.start segment. These draws currently use the fitting observations only. For other families or links, the AR1 correction applies to working residuals used during fitting. It does not specify a joint distribution of actual responses, so sampling produces an error.

Location-scale-shape families mgcv::gaulss(), mgcv::gammals(), mgcv::gumbls(), mgcv::gevlss(), mgcv::shash(), mgcv::twlss() and mgcv::ziplss() support fitting observations, subsets and new covariates. Every distribution parameter is computed from the same joint coefficient draw. Formula offsets and prescribed smooth contributions are retained. Evaluation data need predictors and formula-offset variables, but no observed response. mgcv natively represents the second gaulss() parameter as reciprocal standard deviation: response sampling uses SD, divided by the square root of the sampling weight. Other LSS generators currently ignore sampling weights, following their mgcv implementations. Parameters represented by coefficients vary jointly; other family parameters remain fixed.

Cox survival models require evaluation times and an observation process and do not have a response generator for this interface. Censored-family draws are latent, uncensored responses; reproducing observed censoring requires an observation process and remains unsupported in posterior predictive checks. Grouped-family posterior response draws support fitting observations and supplied data with known family membership. Component nuisance parameters remain fixed. .parameter identifies the component used for each row. Censored grouped components require an observation process; use simulate() for their latent, uncensored responses.

Note

With data = NULL, fitting offsets are retained, including offsets supplied through the fitting function's offset argument. Explicit prediction data follow mgcv::predict.gam(): offsets in formulas are evaluated from the prediction data, while offsets supplied through the fitting function's offset argument are not transferred to new observations. Include offsets in the formula when predicting at new data; the required offset variables must then be present in data.

References

Wood, S.N., (2020). Simplified integrated nested Laplace approximation. Biometrika 107, 223–230. doi:10.1093/biomet/asz044
